36/S0.subgoal: Describe the purpose and types of Contextual Inquiry for gathering user requirements.

36/S1.subgoal: Outline the five systematic stages of the Contextual Inquiry process.

36/S2.subgoal: Detail the necessary planning components for a Contextual Inquiry study.

36/S3.subgoal: Explain the procedures for initiating a Contextual Inquiry.

36/S4.subgoal: Describe the data collection phase of a Contextual Inquiry study.

36/S5.subgoal: Justify the need for formal closure and gratitude when completing a CI study.

36/S6.subgoal: Explain the goal and challenges of data analysis in the Reflection stage of CI.

36/S7.subgoal: Introduce the Affinity Diagram Method as a tool for analyzing CI data.

36/S8.subgoal: Demonstrate how to apply the five steps of the Affinity Diagram Method using a case study.

36/S9.subgoal: Distinguish between preliminary design guidelines and concrete usability requirements derived from CI.

36/S10.subgoal: Explain how to transform broad usability guidelines into specific implementation requirements.

36/S11.subgoal: Illustrate the process of grouping and refining observations to define system requirements using a case study.

36/S12.subgoal: Summarize the core concepts covered in requirement gathering and contextual inquiry.
